report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements are partially defined (core features named) but success criteria, team composition, timeline, and stakeholder sign-off are absent; Hybrid approach allows structured phases with sprint-based execution in Phases 2-3 to accommodate evolving details.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build an internal leave request tracking system enabling employees to submit leave requests, managers to approve/reject via workflow, and automated email notifications on decision.
project_understanding.beneficiary: HR team (50 people) and all employees submitting leave requests
project_understanding.trigger: HR team needs a leave management system; current process implied to be manual or absent
success_definition: Managers can approve or reject requests via dashboard
HR team can view all leave requests
supporting_quotes: build a leave tracker for our HR team
Employees should be able to submit requests
get email notifications when approved or rejected

assumption_log.what: Project deadline is 12 weeks from project start; no deadline provided in input.
assumption_log.why: Internal software projects without explicit deadlines typically follow a standard 10-14 week delivery cycle for TYPE_A tools of this scope (PMBOK 6.4 — Schedule baseline derived from scope definition).
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline requires scope definition and resource availability
assumption_log.consequence: If actual deadline is shorter (e.g., 6 weeks), critical path tasks will not fit; if longer (e.g., 20 weeks), resource allocation and team motivation may suffer from extended timeline.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows decomposition and staffing plan to proceed without stakeholder delay. Risks: if actual deadline is materially different, phases and task sequencing must be re-baselined.

assumption_log.what: Core team composition: 1 Product Manager, 2 Backend Developers, 1 Frontend Developer, 1 QA Engineer; no team specified in input.
assumption_log.why: TYPE_A internal tool with approval workflows and dashboards typically requires backend (workflow engine, database), frontend (UI), and QA; PM is mandatory for scope ownership (PMBOK 9.2 — Resource estimation tied to WBS).
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource estimation and team composition derived from WBS and project complexity
assumption_log.consequence: If actual team is smaller (e.g., 1 developer), timeline doubles or scope must be cut. If team is larger, budget and coordination overhead increase.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows task decomposition and critical path analysis. Risks: if actual team differs, staffing plan and timeline become invalid.

assumption_log.what: Technology stack: Node.js/Express backend, React frontend, PostgreSQL database, SendGrid for email; no stack specified in input.
assumption_log.why: Standard modern stack for internal web applications; widely available expertise in mid-to-large tech companies; reduces technical risk (PMBOK 11.2 — Risk identification before planning baseline).
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Technical risk assessment tied to team experience with chosen stack
assumption_log.consequence: If team lacks experience with chosen stack, Phase 2 duration increases 30-50%; if mandated stack is different, architecture and task list must be re-designed.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows technical task decomposition without re-architecture. Risks: if stack is mandated differently, entire Phase 2 task list becomes invalid.

assumption_log.what: Stakeholder approval of scope is assumed documented or will be obtained before Phase 2 begins; no sign-off mentioned in input.
assumption_log.why: PMBOK 5.4 requires scope baseline to be formally accepted before execution begins; internal projects typically have implicit stakeholder alignment but lack written sign-off (PMBOK 13.2 — Stakeholder requirements documented before execution).
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted requirements; Section 13.2 — Stakeholder engagement before execution
assumption_log.consequence: If scope is not signed off, Phase 1 will extend or Phase 2 will be blocked by scope disputes; rework will consume 20-30% of development effort.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning to proceed with defined scope. Risks: if stakeholder approval is not obtained, project will stall mid-Phase 1.

assumption_log.what: Leave request approval workflow is a simple two-step process: employee submits → manager approves/rejects; no workflow complexity specified in input.
assumption_log.why: Input mentions 'approval workflows' but does not describe escalation, delegation, or multi-level approval; two-step is the simplest defensible workflow for a leave tracker (PMBOK 5.3 — Scope definition).
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.3 — Scope definition requires explicit boundaries; absence of complexity signals simple workflow
assumption_log.consequence: If actual workflow requires escalation (e.g., manager → director → HR), Phase 2 backend complexity increases 40-60%; if delegation is required, UI and database schema must be redesigned.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows backend task decomposition without re-architecture. Risks: if workflow is more complex, Phase 2 effort estimate becomes invalid.

assumption_log.what: Email notifications are sent via third-party service (e.g., SendGrid); no email infrastructure specified in input.
assumption_log.why: Internal projects typically use managed email services rather than building SMTP infrastructure; reduces operational burden and compliance risk (PMBOK 11.2 — Integration risk assessment).
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Integration risk tied to external dependencies; managed services reduce risk vs. custom infrastructure
assumption_log.consequence: If email must be sent via internal SMTP, Phase 2 backend task increases 10-15 hours; if email service is mandated, integration testing in Phase 3 may require additional setup.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: reduces operational complexity and Phase 5 handoff burden. Risks: if internal email is mandated, task estimates and Phase 3 integration testing must be adjusted.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend Developer and Frontend Developer must be allocated full-time across Phases 2-4; PM must maintain continuous oversight; QA Engineer must be full-time in Phases 3-4 to meet 25% QA effort minimum.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: Requirements document finalized and signed off by HR stakeholder
Database schema and API contract approved by tech lead
UI wireframes approved by HR team

tasks.name: Conduct stakeholder requirements workshop with HR team lead
tasks.definition_of_done: Requirements document signed off by HR stakeholder; scope boundaries (e.g., leave types, approval levels, reporting) explicitly documented.

tasks.name: Design database schema for leave requests, approvals, and audit trail
tasks.definition_of_done: ER diagram and schema SQL reviewed and approved by tech lead; supports all leave types and approval states identified in T1.

tasks.name: Define API endpoints and request/response contracts for leave submission and approval
tasks.definition_of_done: OpenAPI/Swagger spec document approved by tech lead; all endpoints (submit, approve, reject, list, get) defined with schemas.

tasks.name: Create UI wireframes for employee request form, manager dashboard, and notification settings
tasks.definition_of_done: Wireframes approved by HR team; all user flows (submit, view status, approve, reject) represented; accessibility considerations noted.

tasks.name: Document approval workflow logic and state transitions
tasks.definition_of_done: State diagram and decision rules documented; edge cases (e.g., overlapping requests, manager absence) explicitly handled or deferred.

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Internal demo completed with HR team

tasks.name: Set up project infrastructure: Git repo, CI/CD pipeline, staging environment
tasks.definition_of_done: Developers can push code and see automated tests run; staging environment accessible to QA team.

tasks.name: Implement database schema and migrations
tasks.definition_of_done: All tables created; migrations tested on fresh database; schema matches approved design from T2.

tasks.name: Implement leave request submission API endpoint and validation
tasks.definition_of_done: POST /leave-requests endpoint accepts employee ID, start date, end date, reason; validates date ranges and conflicts; returns 201 with request ID.

tasks.name: Implement approval/rejection API endpoints and workflow state machine
tasks.definition_of_done: PUT /leave-requests/{id}/approve and PUT /leave-requests/{id}/reject endpoints implemented; state transitions enforced; audit log recorded.

tasks.name: Implement email notification service integration (SendGrid or equivalent)
tasks.definition_of_done: Email sent on request submission (to manager), approval (to employee), and rejection (to employee); email templates configurable; SendGrid API key secured.

tasks.name: Build employee request submission form (React component)
tasks.definition_of_done: Form accepts start date, end date, reason; calls POST /leave-requests; displays success/error message; form validation matches backend.

tasks.name: Build manager approval dashboard (React component)
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard displays pending requests for manager's team; approve/reject buttons functional; request details (employee, dates, reason) visible.

tasks.name: Implement authentication and authorization (employee vs. manager vs. HR roles)
tasks.definition_of_done: Employees can only see/edit their own requests; managers can approve/reject their team's requests; HR can view all requests; role-based access control enforced.

tasks.name: Conduct internal demo with HR team; gather feedback
tasks.definition_of_done: Demo completed with at least 2 HR team members; feedback documented; scope change requests (if any) logged for Phase 3 or deferred.

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases
milestones: Edge cases handled (overlapping requests, manager absence, bulk operations)

tasks.name: Implement request conflict detection (overlapping leave dates)
tasks.definition_of_done: System prevents approval of overlapping requests for same employee; returns 409 Conflict with explanation; UI shows conflicting dates.

tasks.name: Implement manager delegation (if manager is on leave, designate approver)
tasks.definition_of_done: Manager can designate temporary approver; requests route to delegate during manager's leave; audit trail shows delegation.

tasks.name: Test email delivery at scale (50+ employees, concurrent requests)
tasks.definition_of_done: Emails delivered within 5 minutes of approval/rejection; no bounces; SendGrid rate limits respected; retry logic tested.

tasks.name: Conduct security review: authentication, authorization, data protection
tasks.definition_of_done: Security checklist completed: no SQL injection, no XSS, passwords hashed, API tokens secured, HTTPS enforced; findings documented.

tasks.name: Performance testing: response time and database query optimization
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard loads in < 2 seconds with 50 concurrent users; API endpoints respond in < 500ms; database queries indexed; baseline metrics recorded.

tasks.name: Implement audit logging for all leave request actions
tasks.definition_of_done: All actions (submit, approve, reject, delegate) logged with timestamp, user, and change details; audit log queryable by HR.

phases.name: QA & Testing
milestones: User acceptance testing completed with HR team

tasks.name: Execute comprehensive test plan: functional, integration, regression
tasks.definition_of_done: Test cases for all workflows (submit, approve, reject, delegate) executed; critical bugs (P1/P2) resolved; test report generated.

tasks.name: Conduct user acceptance testing (UAT) with HR team and sample managers
tasks.definition_of_done: UAT session completed with 3+ HR team members and 2+ managers; feedback documented; sign-off obtained or issues logged for Phase 4 resolution.

tasks.name: Verify accessibility compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA standard)
tasks.definition_of_done: Automated accessibility scan passed; keyboard navigation tested; screen reader compatibility verified; color contrast meets WCAG AA.

tasks.name: Write user documentation: employee guide, manager guide, FAQ
tasks.definition_of_done: Guides cover request submission, approval workflow, email notifications, troubleshooting; published in HR wiki or knowledge base.

tasks.name: Write admin/operations documentation: deployment, monitoring, troubleshooting
tasks.definition_of_done: Runbook covers deployment steps, environment variables, database backups, common issues; published in internal wiki.

tasks.name: Resolve remaining bugs and performance issues
tasks.definition_of_done: All P1 bugs fixed; P2 bugs resolved or deferred to post-launch; performance targets met; regression tests pass.

tasks.name: Deploy to production: database migration, application deployment, DNS cutover
tasks.definition_of_done: Application running in production; database migrated; all endpoints responding; no errors in logs.

tasks.name: Execute smoke tests in production: submit request, approve, receive email
tasks.definition_of_done: End-to-end workflow tested in production; email delivered; no critical issues found.

tasks.name: Obtain go-live sign-off from HR stakeholder
tasks.definition_of_done: HR stakeholder confirms system is ready for employee use; sign-off documented.

tasks.name: Set up monitoring and alerting for production system
tasks.definition_of_done: Alerts configured for API errors, database issues, email delivery failures; on-call rotation established.

tasks.name: Document post-launch support plan and handoff to operations team
tasks.definition_of_done: Support plan includes escalation path, known issues, workarounds; operations team trained; handoff meeting completed.

risk_register.description: If stakeholder approval of scope is not obtained in writing before Phase 2 begins, then Phase 1 will extend or Phase 2 will be blocked by scope disputes, consuming 20-30% of development effort in rework.
risk_register.trigger: HR stakeholder does not sign off on requirements document by end of Phase 1 Week 1
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule formal requirements review meeting with HR team lead in Phase 1 Day 1; document all decisions in writing; obtain email sign-off before Phase 2 kickoff.
risk_register.contingency: If sign-off is delayed, freeze Phase 2 scope and document all pending decisions as Phase 3 or post-launch items; do not start development on unsigned requirements.

risk_register.description: If core team (2 Backend Developers, 1 Frontend Developer, 1 QA Engineer) is not available full-time, then critical path tasks will slip and timeline will extend by 2-4 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Any developer allocated < 80% to this project or pulled to competing priority
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written commitment from engineering manager for full-time allocation; document in project charter; establish weekly capacity check-ins.
risk_register.contingency: If developer is diverted, immediately escalate to engineering leadership; identify replacement or reduce scope to match available capacity.

risk_register.description: If approval workflow logic is more complex than assumed (e.g., multi-level approval, escalation, delegation), then Phase 2 backend effort increases 40-60% and Phase 3 integration testing extends by 1-2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: HR stakeholder requests features like escalation, delegation, or multi-level approval during Phase 1 or Phase 2
risk_register.mitigation: Document workflow requirements explicitly in Phase 1 Task T5; use state diagram to validate all edge cases; obtain stakeholder sign-off on workflow before Phase 2 begins.
risk_register.contingency: If new workflow requirements emerge, defer to Phase 2 scope change or post-launch; do not expand Phase 2 without extending timeline.

risk_register.description: If email service (SendGrid) integration fails or rate limits are hit, then notifications will not be delivered and user experience will degrade; Phase 3 testing will extend by 1 week.
risk_register.trigger: SendGrid API returns errors during Phase 2 or Phase 3 testing; rate limits exceeded with 50+ concurrent requests
risk_register.mitigation: Set up SendGrid sandbox environment in Phase 1; test email delivery with realistic load in Phase 3 Task T17; implement retry logic with exponential backoff.
risk_register.contingency: If SendGrid is unavailable, switch to alternative email provider (AWS SES, Mailgun) or implement internal SMTP relay; update Phase 3 integration tests.

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 requirements gathering extends beyond 1.5 weeks due to stakeholder unavailability or scope ambiguity, then critical path will slip and Phase 2 start date will be delayed by 1-2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: HR stakeholder unavailable for requirements workshop; scope questions unresolved by Phase 1 Day 5
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule requirements workshop in Phase 1 Day 1; prepare agenda and scope template in advance; set decision deadline for Phase 1 Day 3.
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholder is unavailable, proceed with best-guess scope and document assumptions; plan scope validation session in Phase 2 Week 1.

risk_register.description: If security requirements are not defined (authentication method, data sensitivity, encryption), then Phase 3 security review will uncover gaps and Phase 4 will extend by 1-2 weeks for remediation.
risk_register.trigger: Security review in Phase 3 Task T18 identifies missing authentication, unencrypted data, or authorization gaps
risk_register.mitigation: Define security requirements in Phase 1 Task T1; assume SSO/LDAP authentication and encryption at rest; document data sensitivity (PII: employee names, dates); conduct security review in Phase 3 Task T18.
risk_register.contingency: If security gaps are found, prioritize P1 issues for Phase 4 resolution; defer P2 issues to post-launch; do not deploy to production without P1 fixes.

risk_register.description: If QA Engineer is not allocated at minimum 25% of total development effort (70+ hours), then test coverage will be insufficient and critical bugs will escape to production.
risk_register.trigger: QA effort falls below 70 hours; QA Engineer allocated to competing project during Phase 3-4
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate QA Engineer full-time in Phases 3-4 (minimum 25% of total project hours); establish test plan in Phase 1; execute regression tests in Phase 4.
risk_register.contingency: If QA capacity is unavailable, extend Phase 4 by 1-2 weeks or reduce scope to core workflows only; do not ship without QA sign-off.

risk_register.description: If team has no prior experience with chosen technology stack (Node.js/Express, React, PostgreSQL), then Phase 2 development will extend 30-50% and technical debt will accumulate.
risk_register.trigger: Developers report unfamiliarity with stack; code review reveals architectural issues or performance problems
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm team experience with stack in Phase 1; allocate 2-3 days for spike/POC if stack is new; pair experienced and junior developers.
risk_register.contingency: If team lacks experience, extend Phase 2 by 2-3 weeks or bring in external contractor for architecture guidance; do not proceed with unfamiliar stack without mitigation.

risk_register.description: If HR stakeholder requests scope creep (e.g., reporting, analytics, integration with payroll system), then Phase 2 will extend and timeline will slip by 2-4 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: HR stakeholder requests new features during Phase 2 or Phase 3; scope change requests logged
risk_register.mitigation: Define scope boundaries explicitly in Phase 1 Task T1; document 'out of scope' items (e.g., payroll integration, advanced reporting); establish change control process.
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs, evaluate impact on timeline; defer non-critical features to Phase 2 (post-launch); obtain stakeholder approval for timeline extension.

risk_register.description: If critical path tasks (T1, T3, T5, T8, T12, T15, T18, T21) slip by more than 3 days each, then overall project timeline will extend beyond 12 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Any critical path task takes longer than estimated; dependencies block downstream tasks
risk_register.mitigation: Monitor critical path tasks weekly; identify blockers early; allocate buffer time (15% of total timeline already applied); escalate delays immediately.
risk_register.contingency: If critical path slips, evaluate scope reduction or resource addition; do not absorb delays without timeline adjustment.

staffing_plan.notes: Owns scope, timeline, and stakeholder alignment; must be available for Phase 1 requirements workshop and Phase 4 UAT; 12% allocation is within 10-15% PM oversight rule.
Implements database, API endpoints, approval workflow, email integration, security; full-time in Phases 2-4; critical path tasks T3, T5, T8, T12, T15, T18.
Implements employee request form and manager dashboard; full-time in Phases 2-4; critical path task T12; must ensure WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.
Executes test plan, UAT, accessibility verification, performance testing; full-time in Phases 3-4; 70 hours = 25% of 280 total dev hours (meets PMBOK 8.2 minimum); critical path task T21.
